summary: The bad path acquires BAD_REENTRANT_LOCK but performs the increment, I/O, and unlock outside any try/finally. If any statement between lock() and unlock() throws, the lock is never released, leaking the resource (CWE-404). I wrapped the protected work in a try block and moved unlock() into a finally block, mirroring the safe good1 pattern, so the lock is always released while preserving the increment-and-write behavior.
